name: Shop_ConfirmPartyAction
domain: Draws a yes/no party-action confirmation prompt for one unit (fetched through Func_0808a080), cycling between two message states while polling Func_08015388 for the user's choice, then tears the prompt down.
notes: Clustered against the byte-exact Shop_SelectPartyMember template by the family scan, but the actual behaviour recovered from the retained assembly is a different shop screen: a message/cursor confirmation loop keyed off shop->party_action rather than a party-member list. Recovered independently from the retained owner's control flow, its literal pool (which resolves cleanly to ADDR_03001F2C, the 0x3aa party_action field offset, and four sequential message ids 0xd21/0xd24-0xd25/0xd22/0xd23), and the established ShopRuntime/ShopCursorAnchor layout from shop.h.

The recovered control flow is a near-exact structural match to the reference: matching this candidate's assembly against the reference instruction-by-instruction (candidate-show --align) shows essentially the same opcode sequence and the same operand roles throughout the whole function, with almost every '!' marked difference being a register-number swap (candidate keeps the shop pointer in r8 and list_window in r7; reference keeps shop in r7 and list_window in r8) rather than a structural or semantic disagreement.

This session tried several bounded respellings aimed specifically at flipping that register-bank assignment: (1) storing shop->party_action from an explicit 'party_action' local instead of a literal 0 and moving that local's declaration ahead of 'shop' and 'list_window' in source order (no score change: the compiler's local-initializer ordering already matched regardless of declared order); (2) declaring 'list_window' textually before 'shop' in the local-variable list (no score change); (3) removing the intermediate 'obj' local and inlining the Func_0808a080 call directly into the pointer-chase expression (compiled to byte-identical output, no change); (4) flattening the two nested window-creation fallback 'if's into two sequential 'if's matching the reference's flat bne-to-one-label shape (no score change). None of these moved differing_halfwords off 83 / wrong_instructions off 84, so the register-bank choice is not driven by declaration order, statement nesting, or an extra temporary in this source shape.

This looks like a compiler-internals register-allocation residual, not a remaining source-shape gap: the recovered algorithm, call sequence, argument values, and branch structure all check out against the reference in the aligned diff, and the only persistent disagreement is which of two comparably-live pointer/handle locals (shop vs list_window) the register allocator prefers for a low vs high Thumb register. Closing it likely needs either a genuinely different overall variable/expression shape that changes relative register pressure at the point both locals become simultaneously live, or a permuter-style bounded search rather than further manual respelling.

measured=2026-08-29: swapping the closing UiWindow_Close call order (list_window before shop->money_window, matching a teardown-order hypothesis rather than the source's original money-window-first order) reduced differing_halfwords from 83 to 80 with no change in wrong_instructions or candidate size (364 bytes). This is now the adopted statement order. It is a genuine, narrowly-scoped source correction, not a register-bank workaround.

measured=2026-08-29: on top of the improved 80-diff baseline, 41 additional bounded variants were tried and scored via candidate-show --align --first, none moving the count below 80: reversing/permuting local declaration order (shop/list_window/party_action/cursor_anchor in various orders); swapping cursor_anchor->kind vs ->unknown_00[4] assignment order (alone and combined with decl reordering); nesting vs flattening the two window-creation fallback ifs; reordering shop->cursor.anchor assignment relative to Func_080b0a20 and Func_080b28d4(0xd21); reordering shop->money_window assignment relative to Shop_DrawMoney(); fusing 'shop = SHOP_RUNTIME; shop->party_action = party_action;' into a single comma/assignment expression; introducing intermediate locals for the Func_0808a080 result, the Func_080150f8/Func_080150c8 arguments, the Func_080b280c() result, the &shop->cursor pointer, and the (-32,112) cursor-target coordinates; changing list_window's type to s16 and party_action's type to s8 (both matched their eventual C89 usage but broke codegen entirely, jumping to 166-179 diffs -- rejected); moving Func_080b0204() earlier relative to the UiWindow_Close calls; inverting the Func_080b280c()==0 branch and the loop's break condition; and resetting shop->party_action via the party_action local instead of a literal 0 inside the loop. All either left differing_halfwords unchanged at 80, or regressed it (worst cases 166-179). This reinforces the earlier register-allocation-residual conclusion: the remaining 80-halfword gap is concentrated in the same shop/list_window r7-vs-r8 register-bank swap identified before, and is not reachable through further statement/declaration/temporary-variable respelling in this source shape.

measured=2026-08-29 (second pass, same day): starting from the 80-diff UiWindow_Close-swap baseline above, wrapping the *(u16*)((u8*)shop+0x3a4) = *(u16*)(...) store (the field write fed by Func_0808a080's pointer chase) in a nested block that introduces a local 'u16 *dst' pointer -- i.e. 'dst = (u16*)((u8*)shop+0x3a4); *dst = ...;' instead of the single fused statement -- independently reduced differing_halfwords from 80 to 79 (candidate size unchanged at 364 bytes). This holds whether 'dst' is declared at block scope (nested braces) or hoisted to function scope, and whether it is typed u16* or u8*+cast; all those spellings score identically at 79. This is the new adopted shape. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this change is a mixed result, not an unambiguous improvement -- wrong_instructions rose from 84 to 90 in the same diff. Inspecting the aligned assembly shows why: introducing the extra live pointer temporary at that point changes register pressure enough that the unit_id parameter, previously kept in r5 for the whole function (matching the reference exactly), gets reallocated to r6 instead, producing a NEW register-number mismatch on every later use of that value. So the 'improvement' is a trade: it accidentally realigns a few halfwords elsewhere while introducing a fresh, unrelated r5-vs-r6 divergence. Confirmed this is not free extra-pseudo noise: an unused dummy 'u16 *dummy;' local with no use sites left the score unchanged at 80/83, so the effect requires the temporary to actually be live across the Func_0808a080 call, not merely declared.

measured=2026-08-29 (second pass continued): on top of the new 79-diff baseline, 15 more variants were tried, none improving further: reintroducing an 's32 obj' intermediate for the Func_0808a080 return (alone, and combined with the dst temp) -- no change; four more local-declaration-order permutations (shop-first, cursor_anchor-first) -- no change; wrapping the 0x390 field read (the Func_080150c8 first argument) in an analogous 'u16 *src' temp -- no change; introducing a 'struct ShopCursor *cursor' temp for the repeated '&shop->cursor' argument -- no change; combining the dst temp with an obj temp in the same nested block -- regressed to 80 (worse than the dst-alone 79). The remaining 79-halfword gap is still dominated by the same shop/list_window r7-vs-r8 register-bank swap identified in the first pass, now compounded by the new r5-vs-r6 unit_id split from the dst temp. Given the trade-off (worse wrong_instructions, a new unrelated register mismatch, for a net difference-halfword drop), a future session should weigh whether to keep this shape or revert to the 80-diff/84-wrong-instructions UiWindow_Close-swap-only baseline as the more principled state, and should treat both the shop/list_window and unit_id register-bank splits as one linked allocator-pressure problem rather than two independent ones.
Exact-C adoption remains gated on an independently compiled zero-difference object.
